item.title: MSAF to look into vessel engine failure involving six health workers
item.description: The Maritime Safety Authority of Fiji says it will look into a vessel engine failure involving six health workers and a boat operator in due course after all seven individuals were safely rescued. They say it joins the nation in keeping the six health workers, the boat operator and their families in its thoughts and prayers, while expressing immense gratitude that all seven individuals were safely
item.content:encoded:
The Maritime Safety Authority of Fiji says it will look into a vessel engine failure involving six health workers and a boat operator in due course after all seven individuals were safely rescued.

They say it joins the nation in keeping the six health workers, the boat operator and their families in its thoughts and prayers, while expressing immense gratitude that all seven individuals were safely rescued following their vessel's engine failure.

MSAF says this incident reinforces the importance of maritime safety awareness and compliance for all who rely on sea transport.

The authority says it remains committed to collaborating with the Ministry of Health and the Ministry of Education to strengthen safety practices and improve maritime awareness across communities and frontline personnel.

The authority has also extended its sincere gratitude to the crew of the Lomaiviti Princess 12, along with all agencies and individuals involved in the search and rescue operation, for their swift and decisive response.

MSAF also extends its deepest thoughts to the families and colleagues who endured an anxious wait during this ordeal.

item.title: Damodar unveils $80M Nadi development expected to create more than 680 jobs
item.description: The Damodar Group today unveiled plans for Damodar City Nadi, a development that will bring together shopping, dining, entertainment, accommodation, office space and community facilities in one location. Minister for Finance, Commerce and Business Development Esrom Immanuel says the project will create more than 680 permanent jobs across retail, hospitality, technology, logistics, construction and
item.content:encoded:
The Damodar Group today unveiled plans for Damodar City Nadi, a development that will bring together shopping, dining, entertainment, accommodation, office space and community facilities in one location.

Minister for Finance, Commerce and Business Development Esrom Immanuel says the project will create more than 680 permanent jobs across retail, hospitality, technology, logistics, construction and professional services, while also supporting local businesses and entrepreneurs.

He says the development is a strong vote of confidence in Fiji's economy and demonstrates what can be achieved when the Government and the private sector work together.

Immanuel says the project will also help grow Nadi's 24-hour economy by encouraging visitors to stay longer and spend more, creating new opportunities for local farmers, suppliers, startups and small businesses.

The Minister says the Damodar Group spent more than 16 years studying the Nadi market to ensure the development meets the region's needs rather than simply constructing another commercial building.

Damodar Group Chief Executive Officer Div Damodar says the development will include cinemas, family entertainment facilities, an international food court, restaurants, retail outlets, co-working spaces, a tourism information centre and a branded business hotel.

He says the group aims to create opportunities for surrounding communities by supporting employment, innovation and entrepreneurship alongside the commercial development.

The official launch of the Damodar City Nadi development, including construction details and tenancy plans, is expected to be held in mid-2027.

item.title: Public urged to verify tax certificates amid fraud alert
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 31/07/2026 Members of the public, businesses, government ministries and departments, statutory bodies, financial institutions, and procurement entities are being urged to exercise extreme caution after the Fiji Revenue and Customs Service (FRCS) detected fraudulent Tax Clearance and Tax Compliance Certificates (TCCs), as well as fake letters falsely claiming that legi
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 31/07/2026

Members of the public, businesses, government ministries and departments, statutory bodies, financial institutions, and procurement entities are being urged to exercise extreme caution after the Fiji Revenue and Customs Service (FRCS) detected fraudulent Tax Clearance and Tax Compliance Certificates (TCCs), as well as fake letters falsely claiming that legitimately issued certificates had been cancelled due to a system error, circulating in the country.

FRCS says the documents are fraudulent, unauthorized, and do not originate from the Service.

The Service warns that the creation, distribution, possession, use, or presentation of false tax documents may constitute serious criminal offences and could result in investigation and prosecution under Fiji's laws, with offenders facing substantial fines, imprisonment, or both.

FRCS says it wishes to clarify that it does not cancel, revoke, or invalidate Tax Clearance or Tax Compliance Certificates through informal emails, third-party correspondence, or unverified letters.

The Service adds that any change to the status of a certificate is reflected through its official systems and can be verified via the FRCS Taxpayer Online Services Certificate Validation Portal.

FRCS Chief Executive Officer Udit Singh says the Service takes any attempt to undermine the integrity of Fiji's tax administration system very seriously.

He says the circulation of fake tax certificates and fraudulent cancellation notices is a deliberate attempt to deceive businesses, government agencies, and the public.

Singh says FRCS will not tolerate any activity that compromises the integrity of its systems and processes.

He stresses the importance of verifying certificates through official channels before accepting them as valid and strongly urges all organisations and individuals not to accept any tax certificate at face value.

Singh adds that verification should be undertaken immediately through the official certificate validation portal or directly with FRCS.

He is advising organisations that if they encounter suspicious certificates, they should take immediate precautionary measures.

Singh says where a fraudulent or suspicious certificate is identified, organisations should retain a copy of the document, suspend the relevant transaction or process, and report the matter immediately to FRCS, together with details of the individual or entity that submitted the document.

He warns that those involved in producing, distributing, possessing, or using fraudulent tax documents could face significant legal consequences.

The CEO says any person found producing, distributing, possessing, or using fraudulent tax documents will be subject to investigation and appropriate action under the law.

Singh says these activities may constitute serious criminal offences, and FRCS will work closely with relevant enforcement agencies to ensure those responsible are held accountable.

FRCS encourages anyone who receives a suspicious certificate, cancellation notice, or related correspondence to report the matter immediately.

item.title: 270 potential human trafficking and forced labour cases investigated in Fiji over five years
item.description: Around 270 cases involving workers identified as potential victims of human trafficking or forced labour have been investigated in Fiji over the past five years, as authorities warn that digital recruitment scams are making exploitation more difficult to detect. item.content:encoded:
Around 270 cases involving workers identified as potential victims of human trafficking or forced labour have been investigated in Fiji over the past five years, as authorities warn that digital recruitment scams are making exploitation more difficult to detect.

Speaking during a panel discussion to mark World Day Against Trafficking in Persons at the University of the South Pacific this week, Immigration Manager West Laisa Satala says investigations over the past five years have revealed high levels of exploitation involving people who were promised jobs in Fiji.

She says workers are often lured by promises of decent employment before being exploited.

She says one of the key indicators of human trafficking is where workers are charged recruitment fees before they even begin employment.

Satala says the Ministry of Employment is working closely with other government agencies to investigate these cases and, where necessary, facilitate the return of victims to their countries of origin.

Satala also revealed that authorities are currently investigating an active case involving workers who were recruited online from another country and brought to Fiji under false promises of employment.

Satala adds that the fishing industry remains one of the sectors most vulnerable to exploitation because much of the work takes place at sea, away from public scrutiny.

She says the ministry is working with the International Labour Organization and civil society organisations through a technical working group to address labour exploitation in this sector.

Satala says Fiji is strengthening its response through improved legislation, stronger investigations and closer collaboration between government agencies.

She says work is progressing on Fiji's draft Migration Policy, which includes measures to promote fair and ethical recruitment and address recruitment fees .

Satala says authorities are also developing a mobile application that will allow migrant workers to quickly access information and support services, including contacts for the Police, Immigration and the Ministry of Employment.

She says improving partnerships, prevention, protection, prosecution and public awareness remains central to Fiji's efforts to combat human trafficking.

item.title: Dry weather leaves parts of Taveuni without reliable water for almost a week
item.description: Antornette Vuniuca , Rashika Kumar · 31/07/2026 A resident from Naselesele told fijivillage News the community has had little to no water since last Saturday, raising concerns about the continuing shortage.
item.content:encoded:
Antornette Vuniuca , Rashika Kumar · 31/07/2026

A resident from Naselesele told fijivillage News the community has had little to no water since last Saturday, raising concerns about the continuing shortage.

Responding to questions from fijivillage News, the Water Authority of Fiji says it is aware of the issue and has received a high number of complaints from affected customers.

WAF says the prolonged dry spell has significantly reduced water levels at the Mua raw water source, affecting water production and supply across several communities.

The affected areas include Naselesele Village and Primary School, Valevatu Saioni, Vunikavika, Vunitarawa, New Town, Vatudovia, Vuniweleti, Nagasau, Wiwi Village, Raiwasa Hotel, Taveuni Palm, Maravu Resort, Tight Ridge, Coconut Grove and Matei Point.

WAF says its operations team is carrying out regular valve operations and water rationing to manage the limited supply and ensure water is distributed as fairly as possible among affected communities.

The Authority says normal water supply will only be fully restored once there is sustained rainfall and the island's raw water sources recover.

Questions have also been sent to the National Disaster Risk Management Office on assistance for the people of Taveuni.
